answer: Neighborhood Inlet Ledger. Each new node must attach to an existing node whose inbound link count sits below a fixed ledge; only the graph's summit regions may issue additional attachment slots. Slots are consumed by real traffic volume flowing through the inlet, so creating N identities forces the attacker to sustain N live routing flows that real peers must route through, not just register. Cost per identity: sustained bandwidth and latency overhead proportional to the slots it holds, making mass parallel identities linearly expensive rather than free.
